title: Investigating the chemical link between H<SUB>2</SUB>CO and CH<SUB>3</SUB>OH within the central molecular zone of NGC 253
question: Investigate the physical and chemical properties traced by CH3OH and H2CO in NGC 253 and whether the two species are chemically linked

recipe.goal: extract integrated line intensities at GMC positions
recipe.method: CubeLineMoment spectral and spatial masks give moment 0, 1, 2 maps masked below 3 sigma; transitions selected by SNR and contamination criteria
key_parameters: GMC 5 (absorption) and GMC 10 (non-detections) excluded; 8 GMCs kept
assumptions: Blended lines modelled separately and summed to compare with the measured blended intensity of each group

recipe.goal: convert integrated intensities to K km/s
recipe.method: I(K) = 13.59 (300 GHz / nu)^2 / (theta_max theta_min) I(Jy), with Gaussian beam axes

recipe.goal: non-LTE radiative transfer fit of physical conditions
recipe.method: RADEX via SpectralRadex coupled with Nautilus sampler; fit n_H2, T_kin, column densities of both spin isomers and beam filling factor per GMC
key_parameters: Priors (Table 2): n_H2 1e2-1e8 cm^-3 log-uniform; T_kin 10-800 K uniform; column densities 1e12-1e18 cm^-2 log-uniform; eta_ff 0-1 uniform
T_kin outside the collisional-rate grid (3-250 K CH3OH, 10-300 K H2CO) is clamped to the nearest grid temperature
assumptions: Beam filling factor eta_ff = theta_S^2 / (theta_MB^2 + theta_S^2)

recipe.method: Compare collisional and radiative excitation rates using fitted opacity, density and temperature in each GMC

Divide column densities by H2 column densities from Mangum+2019 (rescaled by 0.63; GMC 1a, 2b, 8a, 9a from Harada+2022), both scaled by the fitted beam filling factor; E- and A- (or o- and p-) combined
assumptions: E- and A- (and o- and p-) column densities are equal within uncertainties so abundances are derived for both forms together

recipe.goal: compare with shock tracers and interpret E/A ratio
recipe.method: Compare n_H2, T_kin and abundances with HNCO, SiO and S-bearing species from earlier ALCHEMI fits; interpret E-/A- column density ratio (EAR) as a probe of formation temperature
assumptions: EAR is fixed at the time of methanol formation; in thermal equilibrium EAR is set by the spin temperature

score_reason: ALCHEMI data are the public large program and the Zenodo intensity table plus stated priors, likelihood, collisional rates and sampler allow rerunning the RADEX fits; but the cube processing, aperture, sampler settings and N_H2 values are not fully given.
rediscovery_reason: The paper's integrated intensities are released, the RADEX plus Nautilus recipe is mostly specified, and the main results are numeric (T_kin, n_H2, column densities, EAR, abundances); full reproduction from cubes would need the ALCHEMI paper.
